seg: Chris — the person the report is about
will be a little late — the reported content
THE POINT — the clause packaged and handed over: reported, not claimed
toiukoto.note: Step 11's という named a thing; add こと and it packages a whole clause — what you were told, or what it all comes down to. Reporting and summarising, one shape.

wr.t: The summarising job opens with つまり: つまり、行けないということですね — 'so what that means is'. The listener does the arithmetic and hands back the total.
wr.jp: つまり、行けないということですね。
wr.en: So what that means is you can't come.

items.q: クリスさんは少し遅れる___です。
items.en: Chris says he'll be a little late — reported, not claimed.
items.why: A clause packaged and relayed → ということだ.

items.q: つまり、行けない___ですね。
items.en: So what that means is you can't come.
items.why: The summary job — the total handed back.

items.q: 大事なのは、続ける___です。
items.en: The important thing is the continuing itself.
items.why: The act itself, packaged as a noun.

items.q: 京都___、お寺ですね。
items.en: Speaking of Kyoto — temples, right?
items.why: A topic picked up, not a clause packaged → というと.

items.q: 新聞によれば、値段が上がる___です。
items.en: According to the paper, prices are going up.
items.why: The written report register — によると pairs with ということだ.

seg: Kyoto — the word somebody just said
THE POINT — the topic handoff: picked up and made the new subject
toiuto.note: How a Japanese conversation changes subject without appearing to: the word is caught mid-air and handed back as the new topic. といえば is its twin.

wr.t: といえば does the same handoff and drifts even more freely into reminiscence: 田中さんといえば — speaking of whom, where IS he lately?
wr.jp: 田中さんといえば、最近見ませんね。
wr.en: Speaking of Tanaka — haven't seen him lately.

items.q: 京都___、お寺ですね。
items.en: Speaking of Kyoto — temples, right?
items.why: The word caught and made the topic.

items.q: 夏___、花火を思い出します。
items.en: Summer makes me think of fireworks.
items.why: The association machine, running on a season.

items.q: 田中さん___、最近見ませんね。
items.en: Speaking of Tanaka — haven't seen him lately.
items.why: The drifting twin — handoff into reminiscence.

items.q: 今日は涼しい___寒いです。
items.en: Today is cold rather than cool.
items.why: A label corrected, not a topic picked up.

items.q: 旅行___、二日だけです。
items.en: A trip — though only two days.
items.why: The word said, then shrunk — といっても.

seg: 'mystery' — the word about to be defined
THE POINT — 'which is to say': holds the word up for definition
something that cannot be explained — the definition
toiunowa.note: Three jobs in one shape: it DEFINES (Xというのは、Yのことです), it gives a REASON in its own sentence, and it PICKS OUT a phrase. The comma and position tell you which is running.

wr.t: As a reason it stands at the head of its own sentence, explaining the one before: 肉は食べません。というのは、菜食主義だからです — the because, given room to breathe.
wr.jp: 肉は食べません。というのは、菜食主義だからです。
wr.en: I don't eat meat. The reason is that I'm vegetarian.

items.q: 「謎」___、説明できないことです。
items.en: A mystery is something that cannot be explained — defining.
items.why: The definition frame: X というのは Y のことだ.

items.q: 肉は食べません。___、菜食主義だからです。
items.en: I don't eat meat. The reason is that I'm vegetarian.
items.why: The reason job, opening its own sentence.

items.q: 「わび」___、どういう意味ですか。
items.en: 'Wabi' — what does that word actually mean?
items.why: The word held up for definition — question form.

items.q: それ___、どういう意味ですか。
items.en: What does that mean? — the casual version.
items.why: って is というのは shrunk for conversation.

items.q: 夏___、花火を思い出します。
items.en: Summer makes me think of fireworks.
items.why: Association, not definition → というと.

seg: cool — the first label, reached for
THE POINT — the label corrected mid-breath: not quite that word
toiuyori.note: Not a comparison of things — a correction of a LABEL. The first word isn't wrong so much as not accurate enough, and the sentence upgrades it in place.

wr.t: むしろ often rides along to push the replacement home: 嫌いというより、むしろ苦手です — not so much dislike as, if anything, no good at it.
wr.jp: 嫌いというより、むしろ苦手です。
wr.en: Not so much dislike as no good at it.

items.q: 今日は涼しい___寒いです。
items.en: Today is cold rather than cool.
items.why: The label upgraded in the same breath.

items.q: 趣味___、仕事です。
items.en: It's work rather than a hobby.
items.why: The word 'hobby' corrected to the truer one.

items.q: 嫌い___、むしろ苦手です。
items.en: Not so much dislike as no good at it.
items.why: むしろ signals the correction's direction.

items.q: 旅行___、二日だけです。
items.en: A trip — though only two days.
items.why: The word kept but shrunk → といっても; というより would replace it.

items.q: 彼は先生___、友だちのような人です。
items.en: He's less a teacher than something like a friend.
items.why: The role-label corrected toward the truth.

seg: a trip — the word that sounds bigger than the thing
THE POINT — 'though I say that': the word kept, and immediately shrunk
only two days — the actual size
toittemo.note: Modesty with a grammar behind it: say the big word, then shrink it before anyone's picture inflates. The word stays; the scale drops.

wr.t: The shrink can be nearly total: 料理といっても、卵を焼いただけ — I say cooking; I fried an egg. The bigger the gap, the more charming the confession.
wr.jp: 料理といっても、卵を焼いただけです。
wr.en: I say cooking; I fried an egg.

items.q: 旅行___、二日だけです。
items.en: A trip — though only two days.
items.why: The word said, then cut down to size.

items.q: 料理___、卵を焼いただけです。
items.en: I say cooking; I fried an egg.
items.why: The near-total shrink.

items.q: 祝日___、特に何もありません。
items.en: A holiday, though nothing special happens.
items.why: The label deflated before expectations form.

items.q: 日本語ができる___、あいさつだけです。
items.en: I 'speak Japanese' — greetings, that is.
items.why: The learner's own most useful sentence.

items.q: 今日は涼しい___寒いです。
items.en: Cold rather than cool.
items.why: Replacement, not shrinkage → というより.

drill.note: Three characters, five jobs: naming (田中という人), packaging (ということだ), picking up (というと), defining (というのは), correcting (というより) — plus the shrink といっても. The surrounding shape always tells you which is running.

items.q: 田中___人から電話がありました。
items.en: A call from a person called Tanaka — naming.
items.why: Bare という names.

items.q: 行けない___です。
items.en: The upshot is he can't go — packaging.
items.why: こと packages the clause.

items.q: 京都___、お寺ですね。
items.en: Speaking of Kyoto — picking up.
items.why: The topic handoff.

items.q: 「謎」___、説明できないことです。
items.en: A mystery IS... — defining.
items.why: The definition frame.

items.q: 涼しい___寒い。
items.en: Cold rather than cool — correcting.
items.why: The label upgrade.

seg: THE POINT — 'according to': you are the pipe, not the source
reported — そうだ closes what によると opened
niyoruto.note: The written twin of Step 15's そうだ: name the source, commit to nothing. によると opens the pipe; そうだ・ということだ・らしい close it.

wr.t: The sentence-end matters: によると expects a reporting close — そうです, ということです, らしいです. Opening the pipe and ending with plain です claims the content as your own.
wr.jp: 新聞によれば、値段が上がるということです。
wr.en: According to the paper, prices are going up.

items.q: 天気予報___、明日は雨だそうです。
items.en: According to the forecast, rain tomorrow.
items.why: The source named, the speaker uncommitted.

items.q: 新聞___、値段が上がるということです。
items.en: According to the paper, prices are going up.
items.why: によれば — the same pipe, ば-flavored.

items.q: 調査___、多くの人が知らないらしいです。
items.en: The survey says most people don't know.
items.why: Surveys are sources; らしい closes the pipe.

items.q: 天気予報によると、明日は雨だ___。
items.en: According to the forecast, it'll rain — the close.
items.why: The pipe must close with a reporting ending.

items.q: 去年___、物価が高くなりました。
items.en: Prices rose compared to last year.
items.why: A baseline, not a source → に比べて.

seg: THE POINT — 'concerning': について one shelf up
nikanshite.note: Same job as について, higher shelf: forms, subject lines, paragraph heads. について there isn't wrong — it's underdressed.

wr.t: Before a noun it becomes に関する: 事故に関する記事 — the formal about, wearing the の-position the way における does.
wr.jp: 事故に関する記事を読みました。
wr.en: I read an article about the accident.

items.q: この件___、質問があります。
items.en: I have a question concerning this matter.
items.why: The formal about, at business height.

items.q: 事故___記事を読みました。
items.en: I read an article about the accident.
items.why: Before the noun 記事 → に関する.

items.q: 日本の文化___勉強しています。
items.en: I'm studying Japanese culture — formally put.
items.why: The dressed-up について.

items.q: この問題___話しましょう。
items.en: Let's talk about this problem — everyday register.
items.why: Conversation keeps について; に関して would overdress it.

items.q: ご質問___は、メールでお願いします。
items.en: Questions on this should go by email.
items.why: The subject-line register in action.

seg: THE POINT — 'compared to': the baseline set, the gap measured
have risen — measured against the baseline
nikurabete.note: より picks a winner; に比べて sets a baseline and measures the gap. Emphasis, not truth-conditions, is the difference.

wr.t: に比べると swaps て for と and reads slightly more analytical — the comparison as observation: 東京に比べると、ここは静かです.
wr.jp: 東京に比べると、ここは静かです。
wr.en: Compared with Tokyo, it's quiet here.

items.q: 去年___、物価が高くなりました。
items.en: Prices have risen compared to last year.
items.why: Last year is the baseline the rise is measured from.

items.q: 東京___と、ここは静かです。
items.en: Compared with Tokyo, it's quiet here.
items.why: に比べると — the analytical cut.

items.q: 前___、ずっと上手になりましたね。
items.en: You've got much better than before.
items.why: The old self as baseline.

items.q: 天気予報___、明日は雨だそうです。
items.en: According to the forecast, rain tomorrow.
items.why: A source, not a baseline.

items.q: 兄___、弟は静かです。
items.en: Compared to his brother, the younger one is quiet.
items.why: The sibling baseline — measured, not ranked.

seg: THE POINT — 'as': two changes tied, moving in step
time feels faster — the second change, traveling with the first
nitsurete.note: Neither half causes the other exactly — they travel together. English spells it out with 'as'; Japanese carries it in one particle.

wr.t: The first half must be a CHANGE: 秋が進む, 年を取る, 練習する. A static state gives につれて nothing to travel with.
wr.jp: 秋が進むにつれて、日が短くなります。
wr.en: As autumn advances, the days grow short.

items.q: 年を取る___、時間が早く感じます。
items.en: As you get older, time feels faster.
items.why: Two changes in step → につれて.

items.q: 秋が進む___、日が短くなります。
items.en: As autumn advances, the days grow short.
items.why: The season moves; the days move with it.

items.q: 練習する___、上手になりました。
items.en: As I practised, I got better.
items.why: Practice advances, skill rides along.

items.q: 去年___、高くなりました。
items.en: Higher, compared to last year.
items.why: A baseline gap, not a joint journey.

items.q: 年を取る___、考え方が変わりました。
items.en: As I aged, my thinking changed alongside it — formal register.
items.why: と共に does につれて's job at a higher altitude.

seg: THE POINT — the smeared range: boundaries vague on purpose
nikakete.note: から〜まで gives two exact points; から〜にかけて gives a stretch with deliberately soft edges — through the night, across the north, from spring into summer.

wr.t: Geography smears the same way: 北海道から東北にかけて — from Hokkaido across the northeast, no line drawn where 'across' ends.
wr.jp: 北海道から東北にかけて、雪が多いです。
wr.en: Heavy snow from Hokkaido across the northeast.

items.q: 今夜から明日___、雨が降るでしょう。
items.en: Rain from tonight through tomorrow.
items.why: Soft edges → にかけて; まで would draw a hard line.

items.q: 春から夏___、花が咲きます。
items.en: Flowers bloom from spring into summer.
items.why: The seasons smear; so does the pattern.

items.q: 北海道から東北___、雪が多いです。
items.en: Heavy snow from Hokkaido across the northeast.
items.why: A geographic smear, not a boundary.

items.q: 九時から五時___働きます。
items.en: I work from nine to five — exact points.
items.why: A timetable has hard edges → まで.

items.q: 週末___、天気が悪くなりそうです。
items.en: The weather looks to worsen into the weekend.
items.why: The forecast's smeared window.

seg: THE POINT — 'together with', in the formal register
tomoni.note: Two jobs: WITH at formal height (家族と共に), and ALONGSIDE for paired change — につれて's job at higher altitude (年を取ると共に).

wr.t: The paired-change reading needs a change on both sides: 技術の進歩と共に、生活が変わった — the advance and the life, moving together on paper.
wr.jp: 技術の進歩と共に、生活が変わりました。
wr.en: Life changed along with advances in technology.

items.q: 家族___暮らしています。
items.en: I live together with my family — formal register.
items.why: The formal WITH.

items.q: 年を取る___、考え方が変わりました。
items.en: As I aged, my thinking changed alongside.
items.why: Paired change at altitude.

items.q: 技術の進歩___、生活が変わりました。
items.en: Life changed along with technology's advance.
items.why: Two changes, formally joined.

items.q: 友だちと一緒___住んでいます。
items.en: I live together with a friend — everyday register.
items.why: 一緒に is the spoken cut; と共に would overdress it.

items.q: 秋が進む___、日が短くなります。
items.en: As autumn advances, days shorten — neutral register.
items.why: The everyday paired-change marker.

drill.note: Six ways to hang a noun off a claim, and English blurs them: によると (source), に関して (formal topic), に比べて (baseline), につれて (proportion), から〜にかけて (smeared range), と共に (with / alongside, formal). Pick the RELATION first.

items.q: 予報___、雨だそうです。
items.en: Source — the forecast said so.
items.why: Named source, uncommitted speaker.

items.q: 去年___、高いです。
items.en: Baseline — measured against last year.
items.why: The gap needs a baseline.

items.q: 年を取る___、変わります。
items.en: Proportion — the two move together.
items.why: Joint motion.

items.q: 春から夏___、咲きます。
items.en: Range — smeared on purpose.
items.why: Soft edges.

items.q: この件___、質問があります。
items.en: Formal topic — as a form would put it.
items.why: The higher shelf of about; について is the everyday one.

seg: Tokyo — the most important member, named
THE POINT — 'starting with': the leader stands for the whole list
in the big cities — the group the leader fronts
wohajime.note: A list that admits it isn't finishing: name the chief member, let it front for the rest. をはじめとする dresses the same move for nouns.

wr.t: Before a noun it becomes をはじめとする: 社長をはじめとする皆様 — the president and, filing in behind the と, everyone else.
wr.jp: 社長をはじめとする皆様に感謝します。
wr.en: My thanks to the president and everyone else.

items.q: 東京___、大都市では家賃が高いです。
items.en: Rents are high in Tokyo and other big cities.
items.why: The chief example fronts the unfinished list.

items.q: 社長___とする皆様に感謝します。
items.en: Thanks to the president and everyone else.
items.why: をはじめとする — the noun-fronting form.

items.q: 日本___、多くの国が参加します。
items.en: Japan among others will take part.
items.why: Japan named first, the list open behind it.

items.q: 若い人___人気があります。
items.en: Popular, mainly among the young — the centre, not the leader.
items.why: Weight, not precedence → を中心に.

items.q: 米___、いろいろな食材を売っています。
items.en: They sell rice and all sorts of other foodstuffs.
items.why: Rice leads; the inventory follows unfinished.

seg: young people — where the weight sits
THE POINT — 'centred on': the concentration named, the edges left open
wochuushin.note: Not the leading example — the centre of gravity. Says where most of it is, without claiming that's all of it.

wr.t: It maps geography and study plans alike: 東京を中心に広がる, 文法を中心に勉強する — the centre can be a city or a curriculum.
wr.jp: 文法を中心に勉強しています。
wr.en: I'm studying with grammar at the centre.

items.q: 若い人___人気があります。
items.en: It's popular, mainly among young people.
items.why: The concentration, not the chief example.

items.q: 東京___広がっています。
items.en: It's spreading outward from Tokyo.
items.why: Tokyo as the centre the spread radiates from.

items.q: 文法___勉強しています。
items.en: Studying with grammar at the centre.
items.why: The curriculum's centre of gravity.

items.q: 東京___、大都市では家賃が高い。
items.en: In Tokyo and other big cities, rents are high.
items.why: A list led, not a weight centred.

items.q: 駅___、店が増えています。
items.en: Shops are multiplying around the station.
items.why: The station is the centre the growth clusters on.

seg: the president — the one being stood in for
THE POINT — 'on behalf of': one takes the other's place
I will give the greeting — humbly, as the stand-in should
nikawatte.note: Two flavours: standing in for a person today (社長にかわって), and replacement over time (手紙にかわってメールが). Both are one thing in another's place.

wr.t: The era-scale replacement is the same grammar: 手紙にかわって、メールが使われています — the letter's seat, taken by email, historically.
wr.jp: 手紙にかわって、メールが使われています。
wr.en: Email has taken the place of letters.

items.q: 社長___、ご挨拶いたします。
items.en: I'll speak on behalf of the president.
items.why: Standing in for a person, today.

items.q: 手紙___、メールが使われています。
items.en: Email has taken the place of letters.
items.why: Replacement over time — same seat, new occupant.

items.q: 父___、お礼を申し上げます。
items.en: On my father's behalf, my thanks.
items.why: にかわり — the tighter written form.

items.q: 病気の先生___、私が授業をします。
items.en: I'll teach the class in place of our sick teacher.
items.why: The stand-in's grammar.

items.q: 去年___、今年は暖かいです。
items.en: Warmer this year, compared to last.
items.why: A baseline — nobody is standing in for last year.

seg: THE POINT — AIMED at: built for them on purpose, one kana from 向き
mukimuke.note: One kana, one real difference: 向き happens to suit; 向け was built for. 子ども向きの本 fits children; 子ども向けの本 was written at them.

wr.t: 向き keeps its literal compass sense too: 南向きの部屋 — a south-facing room. Direction, suitability, and aim, all within one kana of each other.
wr.jp: 南向きの部屋がいいです。
wr.en: I'd like a south-facing room.

items.q: これは子ども___の本です。
items.en: This book was WRITTEN for children.
items.why: Built on purpose for them → 向け.

items.q: この仕事は初心者___です。
items.en: This job happens to suit a beginner.
items.why: It fits, without having been designed to → 向き.

items.q: 南___の部屋がいいです。
items.en: I'd like a south-facing room.
items.why: The literal compass sense keeps 向き.

items.q: 初心者___のコースを作りました。
items.en: We built a course aimed at beginners.
items.why: 作りました — the designing is in the sentence, so the aim is too.

items.q: この味は日本人___かもしれません。
items.en: This flavor may happen to suit Japanese tastes.
items.why: Suits, wasn't engineered → 向き.

seg: THE POINT — ちゅう: in the middle of, and it will stop
polite close — the sign on the door
chuujuu.note: One character, two readings, two meanings: ちゅう is mid-process (工事中 — it will end); じゅう is all-through (一日中 — no gaps).

wr.t: じゅう takes the whole span in one gulp: 一日中雨 — rain all day, no intermissions. The reading is the meaning; misread it and the claim changes size.
wr.jp: 一日中、雨が降っていました。
wr.en: It rained all day long.

items.q: ただいま準備___です。
items.en: We're getting ready — the sign on the door. (reading: ちゅう)
items.why: Mid-process, will end → 〜中（ちゅう）.

items.q: 一日___、雨が降っていました。
items.en: It rained ALL day. (reading: じゅう)
items.why: The whole span, no gaps → 〜中（じゅう）.

items.q: 会議___なので、後でかけ直します。
items.en: I'm in a meeting; I'll call back.
items.why: 会議中 — mid-meeting, ちゅう.

items.q: 「工事中」の読み方は？
items.en: How do you read 工事中 — under construction?
items.why: Mid-process → ちゅう. じゅう would claim the works never pause.

items.q: 「一晩中」の読み方は？
items.en: How do you read 一晩中 — all night long?
items.why: All-through → じゅう.

seg: THE POINT — on the way: the road's middle, doing grammar
tochuu.note: The noun 途中 covers both the road and the task: on the way somewhere, or part way through doing. で marks the event on the way; に marks what's located along it.

wr.t: 途中に takes the locations: 駅へ行く途中に、郵便局があります — the post office sits ON the way; the buying happened AT a point on it (で).
wr.jp: 駅へ行く途中に、郵便局があります。
wr.en: There's a post office on the way to the station.

items.q: 帰る___で、パンを買いました。
items.en: I bought bread on the way home.
items.why: The road's middle — an event en route takes で.

items.q: 会議の___で、電話が鳴りました。
items.en: The phone rang part way through the meeting.
items.why: Part way through the task — 途中 covers it.

items.q: 駅へ行く途中___、郵便局があります。
items.en: There's a post office on the way to the station.
items.why: A thing LOCATED along the way → に; events take で.

items.q: 映画の___で帰るのは、もったいないです。
items.en: Leaving a film midway is a waste.
items.why: Part way through — and the leaving cuts it short.

items.q: 学校へ行く___で、先生に会いました。
items.en: I met my teacher on the way to school.
items.why: An encounter en route.

drill.note: Scope, which English barely marks: who it's for and whether that was intended (向け／向き), who stands in for whom (にかわって), where the weight sits (を中心に), who leads the list (をはじめ), and how much of the span is covered (中 ちゅう／じゅう, 途中). The drill is the map.

items.q: 初心者___のコースです。
items.en: Aimed at beginners — designed for them.
items.why: Intent → 向け.

items.q: 若い人___人気です。
items.en: Centred on young people.
items.why: The weight's address.

items.q: ただいま工事___です。
items.en: In the middle of construction — it will end.
items.why: The sign's ちゅう.

items.q: 社長___、ご挨拶いたします。
items.en: On the president's behalf.
items.why: The stand-in.

items.q: 帰る___で、パンを買いました。
items.en: On the way home.
items.why: The road's middle.

seg: the train's stopped — the alternatives, dying
walk — the one option left standing
THE POINT — nothing for it but: the alternatives ran out, not a rule
shikanai.note: Not must — must says a rule requires it. しかない says the alternatives were checked and are gone. Resignation with a grammar.

wr.t: やるしかない has become the language's shrug-and-begin: no rule, no enthusiasm, just the last option accepted out loud.
wr.jp: やるしかないですね。
wr.en: We'll just have to do it.

items.q: 電車が止まったので、歩く___。
items.en: The train's stopped — nothing for it but to walk.
items.why: Alternatives gone → しかない.

items.q: やる___ですね。
items.en: We'll just have to do it.
items.why: The shrug-and-begin.

items.q: 待つ___ありません。
items.en: There's nothing to do but wait.
items.why: しか + negative — the frame from Step 3, grown up.

items.q: ボタンを押せ___です。
items.en: You just have to press the button — the easy answer.
items.why: One easy action suffices → ばいい, the warm mirror.

items.q: ビザを取ら___なりません。
items.en: You must get a visa — a rule requires it.
items.why: A rule → なければならない; しかない has no rule, only dead ends.

seg: if you press — ば, the conditional from Step 16
THE POINT — that's all it takes: advice that sounds like relief
baii.note: The warm mirror of しかない: the problem shrunk to one action. どうすればいいですか is the question form half of Japan runs on.

wr.t: The question form is the everyday workhorse: どうすればいいですか — what should I do? — the learner's single most useful sentence at any counter.
wr.jp: 分からなければ、聞けばいいですよ。
wr.en: If you don't know, just ask.

items.q: ボタンを押せ___です。
items.en: You just have to press the button.
items.why: One action, and relief → ばいい.

items.q: どうすれ___ですか。
items.en: What should I do?
items.why: The question form of the easy answer.

items.q: 分からなければ、聞け___ですよ。
items.en: If you don't know, just ask.
items.why: The worry shrunk to one friendly action.

items.q: 電車がないので、歩く___。
items.en: No trains — nothing for it but to walk.
items.why: Dead ends, not an easy answer.

items.q: 薬を飲め___んですよ。
items.en: All you need to do is take the medicine.
items.why: The remedy shrunk to a single act.

seg: a child — the most extreme case available
THE POINT — 'even': the extreme case picked to prove the point
sae.note: Sharper than も: さえ picks the limit case. Paired with ば it flips into sufficiency — this one thing, and nothing else, is all that's needed.

wr.t: さえ〜ば is the sufficiency frame: 薬を飲みさえすれば治る — just the medicine, and nothing else, closes the gap. 時間さえあれば is its wistful cousin.
wr.jp: 時間さえあれば、行きたいです。
wr.en: If only I had the time, I'd go.

items.q: それは子供で___分かります。
items.en: Even a child understands that.
items.why: The extreme case as proof → さえ.

items.q: 薬を飲み___すれば、治ります。
items.en: You'll get better if you just take the medicine.
items.why: さえ〜ば — sufficiency: this one thing is enough.

items.q: 時間___あれば、行きたいです。
items.en: If only I had the time, I'd go.
items.why: The one missing ingredient, named.

items.q: ひらがな___読めれば、この本は読めます。
items.en: If you can just read hiragana, you can read this book.
items.why: The minimal sufficient skill.

items.q: 忙しくて、食事___できませんでした。
items.en: So busy I couldn't even eat.
items.why: Even the minimum case failed — さえ with a negative.

seg: THE POINT — 'the thing to do is': advice as general truth, aimed at no one
kotoda.note: Because it never says 'you', it lands as counsel rather than instruction — which is why teachers and coaches live in it.

wr.t: The negative counsels avoidance the same way: 同じ失敗を繰り返さないことだ — the thing is NOT to repeat it. Still aimed at nobody; still heard by everybody.
wr.jp: 同じ失敗を繰り返さないことだ。
wr.en: The thing is not to repeat the same mistake.

items.q: 毎日少しずつ練習する___です。
items.en: The thing is to practise a little every day.
items.why: Counsel stated as general truth → ことだ.

items.q: 同じ失敗を繰り返さない___だ。
items.en: The thing is not to repeat the same mistake.
items.why: The avoidance counsel, same shape.

items.q: まず、休む___ですね。
items.en: First of all, the thing is to rest.
items.why: The coach's opening move.

items.q: 心配する___はありませんよ。
items.en: There's no need to worry.
items.why: ことはない — the release, one lesson over.

items.q: 上手になりたければ、続ける___です。
items.en: If you want to improve, the thing is to keep going.
items.why: Counsel, aimed at no one, heard by you.

seg: worry — the obligation the other person assumed
THE POINT — 'no need': the assumed obligation, removed
warm final よ — reassurance likes it
kotohanai.note: なくてもいい permits not-doing; ことはない says there was never a reason to. Removal, not permission — that's why it reassures.

wr.t: It relieves social debts especially: 謝ることはない — the apology you were winding up to make, waved away before it lands.
wr.jp: 謝ることはないですよ。
wr.en: You don't need to apologise.

items.q: 心配する___はありませんよ。
items.en: There's no need to worry.
items.why: The assumed obligation, removed.

items.q: 謝る___はないですよ。
items.en: You don't need to apologise.
items.why: The social debt, waved away.

items.q: そんなに急ぐ___はない。
items.en: There's no need to rush like that.
items.why: The hurry never had a reason.

items.q: 行けない___はないですが、遅くなります。
items.en: It's not that I can't go — but I'd be late.
items.why: ないことはない — the reluctant yes, one lesson over.

items.q: 怖がる___はありません。犬はおとなしいです。
items.en: No need to be scared — the dog's gentle.
items.why: The fear's obligation, dissolved.

seg: can't go — the flat refusal, about to be refused
THE POINT — the double negative: yes, without enthusiasm
but — the reservation, arriving on schedule
naikotohanai.note: A yes that signals a reservation coming — and the listener will wait for it. The shape IS the hedge.

wr.t: できないこともない swaps は for も and hedges a shade softer still: not un-doable — while the time-cost clause clears its throat.
wr.jp: できないこともないけど、時間がかかる。
wr.en: It's not undoable, but it'd take time.

items.q: 行けない___はないですが、遅くなります。
items.en: It's not that I can't go, but I'd be late.
items.why: The reluctant yes, reservation attached.

items.q: 食べられない___はありません。
items.en: It's not that I can't eat it.
items.why: Yes, faintly — with the face to match.

items.q: できない___もないけど、時間がかかる。
items.en: Not undoable — but it'd take time.
items.why: The こともない shade of the same hedge.

items.q: 心配する___はありません。
items.en: No need to worry — the release, not the hedge.
items.why: ことはない removes; ないことはない reluctantly grants. One negative apart.

items.q: 分からない___はないが、説明が難しい。
items.en: It's not that I don't understand — but explaining is hard.
items.why: Understanding conceded through the double negative.

seg: THE POINT — 'I don't mind if': permission by declining to care
temokamawanai.note: てもいい approves; てもかまわない declines to care. Not politeness — investment. 構う is 'to mind', and the sentence switches minding off.

wr.t: どちらでもかまいません is the pattern's most-used cut: either is fine by me — the choice handed back with a shrug that reads as courtesy.
wr.jp: どちらでもかまいません。
wr.en: Either is fine by me.

items.q: 少し遅れて___いません。
items.en: I don't mind if you're a little late.
items.why: The shrug of non-investment → てもかまわない.

items.q: 窓を閉めても___ませんか。
items.en: Would you mind if I closed the window?
items.why: The asking form — does it trouble you?

items.q: どちらでも___ません。
items.en: Either is fine by me.
items.why: The choice returned unweighted.

items.q: ここに座って___ですか。
items.en: May I sit here? — plain permission.
items.why: Plain approval asks もいい; かまわない adds the shrug.

items.q: 古くても___ません。安いほうがいいです。
items.en: Old is fine by me — cheaper is better.
items.why: The condition waved through uninvested.

drill.note: The dial between forced and free: なければならない (a rule), しかない (alternatives gone), ばいい (the easy answer), てもかまわない (indifference), ことはない (release). The rungs are not interchangeable — read what the situation holds.

items.q: ビザを取ら___なりません。
items.en: A rule requires it.
items.why: Rule → なければならない.

items.q: 電車がないので、歩く___。
items.en: No rule — no options.
items.why: Alternatives ran out.

items.q: 心配する___ありません。
items.en: Released — there was never a need.
items.why: The obligation dissolved.

items.q: 聞け___んですよ。
items.en: Just ask — that's all it takes.
items.why: The easy answer.

items.q: 少し遅れて___。
items.en: Fine by me if you're a bit late.
items.why: Indifference, offered kindly.

seg: he — the subject of the impossible claim
THE POINT — 'no way': not false, IMPOSSIBLE — no route to it being true
wakeganai.note: に違いない's exact opposite face: where that closed the guess upward, わけがない closes it downward — no route exists by which this could be true.

wr.t: The reasoning is the content: わけ is the route, が is its subject, ない erases it. こんな簡単な問題、間違えるわけがない — the route to error does not exist.
wr.jp: こんな簡単な問題、間違えるわけがありません。
wr.en: No chance of getting a question this easy wrong.

items.q: 彼が知っている___がない。
items.en: There's no way he knows.
items.why: The route to it being true, erased → わけがない.

items.q: こんな簡単な問題、間違える___がありません。
items.en: No chance of getting this wrong.
items.why: Impossibility, argued from reason.

items.q: そんなに安い___がないでしょう。
items.en: There's no way it's that cheap.
items.why: The price refuses the route to plausibility.

items.q: みんなが働いているので、帰る___にはいきません。
items.en: I can't very well leave while everyone's working.
items.why: わけにはいかない — socially impossible, one lesson over.

items.q: 高いものがいい___限りません。
items.en: Expensive doesn't always mean good.
items.why: Not-always is とは限らない; わけがない would claim never-possible.

seg: みんなが働いているので
THE POINT — can't very well: able in body, forbidden in society
wakeniwaikanai.note: Not ability — できない covers that. This is the thing you could do and socially cannot: leave early, refuse the toast, say the true sentence out loud.

wr.t: The negative flips it into social obligation: 行かないわけにはいかない — not-going is the thing that's impossible, so going becomes duty with a bow on it.
wr.jp: 約束したので、行かないわけにはいかない。
wr.en: I promised, so I have to go.
wr.hl: ないわけにはいかない

items.q: みんなが働いているので、帰る___にはいきません。
items.en: I can't very well leave while everyone's working.
items.why: Physically able, socially barred.

items.q: 約束したので、行かない___にはいかない。
items.en: I promised, so I have to go.
items.why: Not-going is what's impossible — duty by double negative.

items.q: ここで諦める___にはいかない。
items.en: I can't afford to give up here.
items.why: The stakes forbid it, not the body.

items.q: この漢字は難しくて、読む___ができません。
items.en: This kanji is too hard — I can't read it.
items.why: Plain ability → ことができない; society has no opinion here.

items.q: 先生にもらった本ですから、捨てる___にはいきません。
items.en: My teacher gave me this book — I can't very well throw it away.
items.why: The giver's shadow forbids the bin.

seg: expensive means good — the rule of thumb
THE POINT — 'not necessarily': always denied, usually conceded
towakagiranai.note: The politest disagreement in the language: it concedes the general case while denying the ALWAYS. 必ずしも loves to walk in front of it.

wr.t: 必ずしも is its natural adverb: 必ずしも成功するとは限らない — not necessarily, formally hedged, the rule punctured without being torn.
wr.jp: 必ずしも成功するとは限らない。
wr.en: It won't necessarily succeed.

items.q: 高いものがいい___限りません。
items.en: Expensive doesn't always mean good.
items.why: The always punctured, the usually conceded.

items.q: 日本人が全員寿司を好きだ___限らない。
items.en: Not every Japanese person likes sushi.
items.why: The generalization trimmed to honest size.

items.q: 必ずしも成功する___限らない。
items.en: It won't necessarily succeed.
items.why: 必ずしも announces the puncture.

items.q: 彼が知っている___がない。
items.en: There's NO WAY he knows — total, not partial.
items.why: Impossibility is わけがない; とは限らない only denies the always.

items.q: 有名な店がおいしい___限らない。
items.en: Famous doesn't always mean delicious.
items.why: The diner's own precision instrument.

seg: finish — the ます-stem そう rides on
THE POINT — the appearance is of it NOT happening, with a little despair
soumonai.note: Not そうじゃない (denying the appearance) — そうもない reads the appearance itself as negative: it visibly isn't going to. The despair is included.

wr.t: そうにない is the same reading with に: 雨はやみそうにない — the rain, visibly uninterested in stopping. Both cuts survive; both carry the sigh.
wr.jp: 雨はやみそうにないですね。
wr.en: The rain doesn't look like stopping.

items.q: 今日は終わり___もありません。
items.en: It doesn't look like finishing today.
items.why: The appearance of not-happening → そうもない.

items.q: 雨はやみ___にないですね。
items.en: The rain doesn't look like stopping.
items.why: そうにない — same sigh, に-cut.

items.q: 彼は来___もない。
items.en: He doesn't look like coming.
items.why: The horizon, read and found empty.

items.q: この仕事は五時までに終わり___にありません。
items.en: No sign of this work finishing by five.
items.why: The visible trajectory, despaired of.

items.q: おいし___なケーキですね。
items.en: That cake looks delicious — the positive そう, for contrast.
items.why: Same そう, positive face — the appearance affirmed.

drill.note: Four noes English says with one word: the fact is false (じゃない), the inference doesn't follow (わけではない), it's not always true (とは限らない), it's not possible at all (わけがない). Wrong pick sounds confused, not rude — the drill is the sorter.

items.q: 嫌いな___ではありません。よく食べますよ。
items.en: It's not that I dislike it — the inference denied.
items.why: The conclusion drawn, refused.

items.q: 安いものが悪い___限らない。
items.en: Cheap isn't always bad — the always denied.
items.why: Partial, polite puncture.

items.q: 彼が知っている___がない。
items.en: No way he knows — the possibility denied.
items.why: The route erased entirely.

items.q: 帰る___にはいきません。
items.en: Can't very well go home — the social no.
items.why: Able, and barred.

items.q: 終わり___もない。
items.en: Doesn't look like ending — the visible no.
items.why: The appearance itself reads negative.
